approach: Derive the hold from committed records and write nothing. In scope_guard.rs add `RequestRecord.verified_unlanded` (a job verified with a pass but never closed: Blocked, or Dispatched with a passing verification and no finished attempt). It is only a flag and never enters `attempts`, so T1 to T5 do not change. New `non_landed_attempts(requests, line, live)` counts through `group_lines`/`line_attempts`: the line's Rejected and Failed attempts, plus every `verified_unlanded` request on the line that `live` does not report running. Environment attempts are ignored and a line with an Accepted attempt counts 0. New `hold_reason(requests, job_id, live)` finds the job's line with `group_lines` and returns a reason at 2 or more. This revision drops the earlier own-job skip and the supersession test. Every verified-but-not-landed job counts, including the job the drain itself is about to redo, so a collision-only chain [X not landed, X2 not landed] is held at two (revision finding 1), not three. drain.rs gets a default `Steps::awaiting(jobs)`. `RealSteps::awaiting` reaps the registry, builds `request_records` once and calls `hold_reason` with `self.athena.running`. It is asked in `Drain::prepare` BEFORE the planning read loop, so a held item is never read (finding 2), and at the top of each `Drain::attempts` iteration after the pause check (new `ItemEnd::Awaiting`). It is recomputed on every run.

decisions.choice: Count every verified-but-not-landed job (Blocked, or Dispatched with a passing verification and no finished attempt) that `live` does not report running as one non-landed attempt, with no exemption for the item's own job and no requirement that a later request supersede it. A line is held at 2 or more counted attempts.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: Landing::NotLanded writes no closing record (drain.rs:1826-1829), so the job stays dispatched with a passing verification, and `interrupted_work` (steward.rs:447-480) plus `RealSteps::queue` (drain.rs:4210-4218) hand it back to the drain as an interrupted item. With the earlier own-job skip, [X not landed, X2 not landed] with item X2 counted only X, so a third attempt ran. Criterion 2 names exactly two verified-but-not-landed attempts. Counting the own job as well holds that line at two, and it is the simplest rule. It also makes the hold uniform across the item's iterations: the count cannot change because the drain started redoing a job. A waiting pull request that later merges makes the line Accepted, so the hold lifts on the next run because it is recomputed from records.

rejected.option: Skip the item's own job (previous plan)
rejected.why: Finding 1: a collision-only chain gets a third attempt, which narrows criterion 2.

rejected.option: Skip the own job only when it is the line's only non-landed request
rejected.why: In the loop the drain's own first retry X2 is then a second non-landed request, so X would be counted from the second iteration on. This gives the same result as no skip, with an extra rule to test.

rejected.option: Ask the lander or the pull request whether the own job is waiting to merge before counting it
rejected.why: It needs a network call on a pure record rule, and the records already say verified but not landed. The Landing::Waiting path writes nothing (drain.rs:1935).

rejected.option: Keep the second attempt for a lone waiting item and record three attempts for collision chains
rejected.why: It contradicts the request, which is to stop once a line has two attempts that did not land, and it narrows criterion 2.

rejected.option: Count an open job only when Blocked
rejected.why: Criterion 2 says 'still open or blocked'. A collision job can be Dispatched with a passing verification.

decisions.choice: Count a line's attempts with new `scope_guard::non_landed_attempts`, built on `group_lines` and `line_attempts`. `hold_reason` is a pure function over `&[RequestRecord]` and a `live` closure.
decisions.reason: The brief forbids a second line-grouping function. A pure function needs no git, so drain tests can feed real `RequestRecord` values. Liveness is a closure, as `interrupted_work` takes `running` (steward.rs:447).

rejected.option: Count inside drain.rs from the run's job list
rejected.why: It does not see earlier runs and would be a second grouping.

rejected.option: Write a pause or flag file
rejected.why: That feeds `athena status` and `line_pause`. Release is a named follow-up.
scope_guard's request functions take records only. The registry lives on `Athena`.

decisions.choice: Represent the verified-but-closed-less job as a bool on `RequestRecord`, not as an `AttemptRecord` or a new `Verdict`.
decisions.reason: `counted()` treats every verdict except Environment as an attempt for T1, T2 and T5, and T3 sums cost over attempts (scope_guard.rs:222-243). A variant or extra attempt would change T1 to T5, which is out of scope. `RequestRecord` literals exist only at scope_guard.rs:658 and in the `req()` helper near 1789.

rejected.option: Make `verdict_of` return Failed for Blocked and open jobs
rejected.why: It is the same signal change, and it turns a job awaiting `go` into a failure.

decisions.choice: Ask the hold in `prepare` right after `paused` is computed and before the planning read loop (drain.rs:2126-2138), and at the top of the `attempts` loop after the pause check (drain.rs:1875). Held ids are merged into the same stopped set the read loop already skips (`paused.contains_key(&id)` at 2136). A separate `by_hold` set records which ids came from the hold. A new `ItemEnd::Awaiting` ends the item.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the held map is built only after the read loop (drain.rs:2202), so the hold must be known before the loop or an unread item on a held line is read and paid for. The in-loop check stops the second attempt and a later drain run. A fresh item with no counted attempts still gets both attempts.

rejected.why: An unread item on a held line would still be read in planning.
The count changes during a run.

rejected.option: Fill `by_hold` only when building the held map (after the loop)
rejected.why: The read loop at 2130-2138 would not skip held items (finding 2).

decisions.choice: `paused` is asked first and `awaiting` only for ids not paused. Dependents carry the cause at every level of the dependents loop (drain.rs:2206-2223): 'its line is awaiting diagnosis' when `on` is in `by_hold`, and the unchanged 'its line is paused' otherwise.
decisions.reason: With `by_hold` empty the text is byte-identical, so existing paused tests keep their exact text. Reusing the held map reuses `pass_over_paused`, the `first_paused` filtering and the `athena plan` held listing.

rejected.option: A second map and printer for holds
rejected.why: It duplicates held plumbing and risks double lines.

decisions.choice: Environment stops are never counted and a line with an Accepted attempt is never held. The reason text says 'awaiting diagnosis', names the line and the counts, and says the drain will not retry it. It never says 'paused' or that a diagnosis job exists.
decisions.reason: This follows `counted()` and `done()` (scope_guard.rs:222-233) and the request. The pause text would send the operator to delete a pause file that does not exist.

rejected.why: It would hold lines for a full disk or an expired login.
It is misleading, and the release path is a follow-up.

decisions.choice: No request-text or reading rule is added or changed, so the refusal corpus gets no new case.
decisions.reason: The rule reads job records only. 'try again on <job>' is still parsed only by the existing `retried_job`. Input forms of the rule are record shapes, tabled in the tests: one Failed, two Failed, Rejected+Failed, Environment stops, Accepted in line, Failed+verified, two verified, lone verified, live. `cargo test --locked` runs the corpus test, so an accidental effect shows.

rejected.why: The corpus tests request and reading text, and nothing in the hold reads either.

Add default `Steps::awaiting` and `RealSteps::awaiting`; ask the hold in `prepare` before the read loop and merge it into the stopped set with its cause carried to dependents; hold check at the top of `Drain::attempts`; `ItemEnd::Awaiting` and its `finish` arm; module-doc bullet.
Extend `Stub` with `records` and `track_runs` and implement `awaiting` through production `hold_reason`; add `awaiting_diagnosis_*` tests and one RealSteps test.

risks.risk: A pull request waiting to merge, or a job not landed after two landing tries, now counts as a non-landed attempt, so the drain gives an interrupted waiting job one retry, not two as today (revision finding 1 and the prior waiting-to-merge concern).
risks.mitigation: This is the rule the criterion names (two verified-but-not-landed attempts, one still open). It is stated in the changelog and the hold reason names the counts. If the pull request later merges, `athena land` closes the job Accepted and the hold lifts on the next run, because the count is recomputed from records. A Stub test pins the one-retry behavior. The question is put to the user.

risks.risk: A job that is running in another process but already verified could be counted as an unlanded attempt.
risks.mitigation: `hold_reason` takes a `live` closure and `RealSteps::awaiting` passes `self.athena.running` after reaping the registry as `queue()` does (drain.rs:4210). A unit test shows a live job is not counted.

risks.risk: An interrupted item on a line that already has two non-landed attempts is held and not retried, though the drain retried it before.
risks.mitigation: That is the rule's intent; no read or run is paid. The reason names the line and counts. Stub tests cover [Failed, Failed, X interrupted] and [X, X2 interrupted].

risks.risk: An existing real-steps or lifecycle test has a line that already reaches two counted attempts and then expects a retry, so it now fails.
risks.mitigation: The real-steps drains that retry use environment stops, interrupted jobs without a passing verification, or fresh items, which are not counted or start at zero. The producer runs the full `cargo test --locked` and changes only a test whose expectation is that retry.

risks.risk: A held line has no release: it stays held until it lands or the request is rephrased.
risks.mitigation: Stated scope. The reason names the line and says the drain will not retry it. Nothing is written, so no cleanup is owed.

risks.risk: The new `RequestRecord` field breaks other struct literals.
risks.mitigation: Searched all crates: literals exist only at scope_guard.rs:658 and the `req()` helper. The compiler flags any other.

risks.risk: The hold at two attempts overlaps with the T1 flag at three and the T4 pause at two same-criterion rejections, so operators could see two reasons.
risks.mitigation: A pause is reported first and the hold is asked only for jobs not paused. The hold text says 'awaiting diagnosis', never 'paused'.
`queue()` already reaps before `running()` (drain.rs:4210) for the same reason, so a dead process is not taken as live.

A second `drain::drain` on the same stub does the same. `drain::plan` lists a in `plan.refused` with that reason. (b) One earlier Failed attempt, `track_runs`, outcomes Rejected then Landed: the log is exactly `read a`, `run a`, with no `reread a`, and the item is passed over with the reason. Two `drain::drain` runs leave `fx.head()` unchanged and each prints 'passed over: line <job> is held, awaiting diagnosis'. demonstrations.observes: (a) Failed plus open: c1 Failed; c2 (retry of c1) `verified_unlanded`; queued item a retries c2. The log is empty and a is passed over as held. (b) Two open collision jobs, both ways the drain meets them. Case 1: c1 and c2 `verified_unlanded`, with a person's retry item a on c2: held. Case 2, the finding-1 shape: X `verified_unlanded` and X2 `verified_unlanded` (retry of X), item X2 in `interrupted`. The log is empty and X2 is passed over as awaiting diagnosis. Without the own-job skip the drain no longer makes the third attempt X2-retry. (c) A lone waiting item X (`verified_unlanded`, interrupted, no other attempt) is retried once: with `track_runs` and outcomes Failed then Landed the log is `reread X`, `run X-retry`, then the item is passed over as awaiting diagnosis (X plus the failed X-retry make two). There is no second `reread`. The changelog states this. (d) [F1 Failed, X waiting interrupted]: held up front, empty log. (e) A `live` closure reporting c2 running makes the count 1 (unit test). Unit tests: `hold_reason` Some for [Failed, verified], [verified, verified] and [Failed, Failed, verified]; None for [verified] alone and for an unknown job. Derivation test with `rig`: after a passing job, an in-memory edit sets `outcome.state` to Blocked, then removes the outcome. `request_records` gives `verified_unlanded == true` and no attempt for both. It gives false when the verification is removed, and false when an attempt exists. `evaluate_before_attempt` over `line_attempts` is identical with and without the flag.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without counting verified-but-not-landed jobs, the collision lines have 0 or 1 counted attempts. The drain logs `read a` and `run a`, and `hold_reason` returns None. With the earlier own-job skip, (b) case 2 counts only X and the drain makes the third attempt X2-retry, so its empty-log assertion fails.

demonstrations.seam: Production `non_landed_attempts` and `hold_reason` through `drain::drain` with the `Stub.records` fixture (step 6). Unit tests build `RequestRecord` with the existing `req()` and `att()` helpers (scope_guard.rs, near 1773 and 1789). `req()` is updated in step 1.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the whole workspace.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check
demonstrations.observes: All pass. This includes the unchanged Stub drain tests (the default `Steps::awaiting` holds nothing), the RealSteps tests that exercise the real hook (flagged and paused tests where both attempts are still made, the interrupted-job tests at tests/drain.rs:5074-5268, the refusal corpus test). The RealSteps interrupted tests pass because their killed jobs have no passing verification and no closed attempt, so the count is 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missed `RequestRecord` literal, an unused import, or an existing test whose line now reaches two counted attempts and expects a retry would fail here.
demonstrations.seam: The whole workspace suite; nothing is injected.

demonstrations.method: Diff and search check that counting goes through the existing grouping.
demonstrations.observes: `non_landed_attempts` calls `line_attempts(requests, line)`, `hold_reason` calls `group_lines(requests)`, and `RealSteps::awaiting` calls `request_records` then `hold_reason`. Grep for `fn .*group` and union-find (`parent`) in the changed files finds only the existing `group_lines`.
demonstrations.fails_without: A second grouping function in the diff would show in the same search.

demonstrations.observes: One bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`, before `### Changed`. It says the drain holds a line after two attempts that did not land (rejected, failed, or verified but not landed; environment stops not counted), does not retry it, passes it over with 'awaiting diagnosis', writes nothing and recomputes from records. It also says a job waiting to merge or not landed counts as one of the two, even when the drain would itself retry it after an interruption, and that a landing makes the hold lift. It names no diagnosis job, schema, status display or line field.
demonstrations.fails_without: A bullet that mentions those would show in the diff.

demonstrations.observes: Only CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs are listed. No athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows or prompt file. The scope_guard.rs diff touches none of `T1_*` to `T5_*` or `t1_retries`, `t2_plan_growth`, `t3_cost`, `t4_rejections`, `t5_time`.
demonstrations.fails_without: An edit to a governance or prompt file would appear in the stat.

open_questions: User: Is it acceptable that a job verified but not landed (waiting to merge, or not landed after two landing tries) counts as one of the two attempts even when the drain would itself retry it after an interruption? The result is that a lone waiting job gets one drain retry instead of two, and a line of two such jobs is held at two. That is what criterion 2 asks, and it is a change from today.

User: There is no command to release a held line in this job (release is a named follow-up). Is it acceptable that the operator escapes a hold only by asking in new words, which starts a new line, until that follow-up exists?
